research_question: Does the frozen paired block and seed bootstrap attain nominal simultaneous coverage and detect known HJ-type distance gaps?
changes_from_parent: Bounded inference calibration only: analytic known-truth moment DGP; no model training, no new market, no empirical retuning.
estimand: All 15 pairwise differences of population HJ-type distances averaged over five fixed seed models. True distances: dimensions 1..5 equal baseline+gap, K8 equals baseline. Candidate labels index fixed models, not true structural dimension.
dgp: Gaussian stationary AR(1) pricing-moment vectors in whitened payoff coordinates; time dependence phi, common/dimension/seed covariance shares .5/.3/.2. All 5 seed model means are deterministic rotations with exactly equal norm within K. Moment dimension 74 or an isometric rank-4 subspace of 74. Annualized distance sqrt(12)*norm(E[mR] whitened). Monthly noise energy fixed at 4*sigma^2 across ranks. No claim of a coherent full return/SDF structural DGP or empirical power calibration.
procedure: Exactly reproduce V003 statistic: common 12-month circular blocks, five shared resampled seed indices, mean of seed-specific pricing distances, pair differences, ddof=1 bootstrap standard error, .95 max absolute standardized bootstrap-minus-observed quantile, symmetric simultaneous intervals. The norm is taken before seed averaging. Validation coefficients/weight held fixed.
primary: At T=120, rank74, phi 0 and .5: familywise false rejection under equal distances and simultaneous coverage across all 15 pairs; detection of a truly better K8 for gaps .5,1,2. All other scenarios are fixed sensitivity/stress cases.
reported_metrics: familywise false rejection among truly zero pairs (nominal .05)
probability of detecting any true gap
probability of detecting all five K8 advantages
point-winner and conditional bootstrap winner frequencies
mean interval width and finite-sample norm bias
95% Wilson Monte Carlo intervals based on 400 independent outer repetitions
interpretation_rules: Report rates and Monte Carlo intervals, never infer equality from non-rejection.

Flag material undercoverage if coverage Wilson upper bound <.90; flag material false rejections if false-rejection Wilson lower bound >.10. These tolerances are warning thresholds, not proof of exact calibration.
The zero-distance cases deliberately test a nondifferentiable norm boundary; failures restrict conclusions and are not a tuning target.
Synthetic gaps are controlled norm units; results are not a power estimate for observed US equity differences.
Stable bootstrap winners and non-significant intervals can coexist. A winner is not an estimator of structural K.
stopping_rule: Run all 30 cells x400 outer repetitions once with 1999 inner draws. Do not enlarge the grid or change block lengths/method after inspecting outcomes. Technical corrections require separate immutable version. Any inferential limitation is reported; no automatic search for a method yielding empirical significance.
limitations: Post-result audit specified after observing V003, not fresh empirical confirmation.
Conditional on fixed model means and a fixed pricing weight; does not cover training, hyperparameter selection or estimated validation weights.
Gaussian moment-level simulation does not establish universal coverage or empirical equivalence.
Only 400 Monte Carlo repetitions per cell: nominal .05 probabilities have about one percentage point standard error.
No new model training, financial dataset, trading strategy or sealed-period access.
